Module 4 · 150–190 minutes

Planar surface codes: boundaries and patches

Assumes: stabilizer checks, CSS rank and Pauli frames (Module 2) · toric stars and faces, string syndromes and logical crossings (Module 3) · distance as the least weight of a nontrivial logical Pauli (Module 3)

Requires: The toric code: strings, logicals and matter · Enables: qLDPC codes: sparse checks, long connections, Measuring a surface code: circuits, detectors and Google's memory experiments

By the end, you can
  • Explain the torus-to-patch construction, identify truncated checks and allowed endpoints, and derive planar counts.
  • Derive rotated counts and distance and read distance-3, -5 and -7 patch anatomy, including Google's hardware count.
  1. 4.1 · From torus to plane: boundaries and what may end where
  2. 4.2 · The rotated code: a smaller code, not a relabeling
  3. 4.3 · Anatomy of distance-3 and distance-5 patches
  4. 4.4 · Reconstruct and transfer

Can we cut open a toric code and still keep an encoded qubit?

On the torus, a string ends where a check detects it. Opening an edge of the lattice changes which checks remain. Follow a Z error toward an edge. If the star that would detect its endpoint is absent, extending the string can remove the last flag there.

That observation leaves a counting problem. Removing qubits also removes or changes checks. We must count their independent constraints before deciding how many logical qubits remain. Begin with the open grid below. Find its data qubits, then inspect the checks beside a free tip.

Allow 150–190 minutes for the core reading, lab and selected practice. A natural break comes after the rotated-code construction.

§

4.1 · From torus to plane: boundaries and what may end where

On the torus, every string endpoint raised a flag. Where can an endpoint hide once the lattice has an edge?

The grid below has open tips above and below its retained vertices. We will follow an error to a tip and inspect the checks there.

The retained stars and faces share zero or two qubits, so the overlap rule makes them commute.

In panel (a), apply Z on the central edge v(1,1)v(1,1)v(1,1). Each trial starts from a code state, with all checks reading +1+1+1. We use ideal Pauli operations and perfect check readings. A flag means a reading of −1-1−1.

The Z-string rule counts selected edges at each star. Stars A(1,1)A_{(1,1)}A(1,1)​ and A(1,2)A_{(1,2)}A(1,2)​ each meet the selected edge once, so both become flagged. Each failed X star is an e excitation. The neighboring Z faces commute with this Z and stay positive.

Panel (b), “Add Z toward the top,” extends the route onto v(1,0)v(1,0)v(1,0). The old upper star now meets two selected edges. Its two sign reversals restore +1+1+1. The lower star still meets only v(1,1)v(1,1)v(1,1), so its e remains. At the new upper end, (1,0)(1,0)(1,0) has no X detector. The endpoint leaves without raising another flag Topological quantum memory, PDF p. 7, Fig. 5 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1063/1.1499754.

The highlighted B(0,0)B_{(0,0)}B(0,0)​ remains a positive truncated check. A Z-boundary is a side named for its retained truncated Z checks. The missing star explains why a Z endpoint can disappear there.

Panel (c) starts afresh with every check positive. Apply X on v(1,1)v(1,1)v(1,1). The X-string rule counts selected qubits around each face. Faces B(0,1)B_{(0,1)}B(0,1)​ and B(1,1)B_{(1,1)}B(1,1)​ each meet this qubit once and become flagged. A failed Z face is an m excitation. The route joining their centers crosses the physical edge qubit.

Panel (d), “Add X toward the left,” adds X on v(0,1)v(0,1)v(0,1). Face B(0,1)B_{(0,1)}B(0,1)​ now meets two selected qubits and returns to +1+1+1. Its partner B(1,1)B_{(1,1)}B(1,1)​ still meets only the seed qubit and stays failed. The next face, B(−1,1)B_{(-1,1)}B(−1,1)​, is absent beyond the left edge.

The retained side star is A(0,1)=Xh(0,1)Xv(0,0)Xv(0,1)A_{(0,1)}=X_{h(0,1)}X_{v(0,0)}X_{v(0,1)}A(0,1)​=Xh(0,1)​Xv(0,0)​Xv(0,1)​. Its X factors commute with the X error. An X-boundary is a side named for its retained truncated X checks. This side absorbs the m endpoint while the bulk partner remains visible.

Anyon condensation means that an excitation can enter a boundary without leaving a local failed check there. Here e enters a Z-boundary, and m enters an X-boundary Quantum codes on a lattice with boundary, PDF pp. 5-6 Original source ↗.

Does a smooth side erase a vertex defect?

Use the open patch, with all checks initially +1+1+1. Apply Z on v(1,1)v(1,1)v(1,1) and then on h(0,1)h(0,1)h(0,1). The resulting simple path joins bulk vertex (1,2)(1,2)(1,2) to smooth-side vertex (0,1)(0,1)(0,1), away from a corner. Its boundary star is A(0,1)=Xh(0,1)Xv(0,0)Xv(0,1)A_{(0,1)}=X_{h(0,1)}X_{v(0,0)}X_{v(0,1)}A(0,1)​=Xh(0,1)​Xv(0,0)​Xv(0,1)​. How many X checks remain flagged?

Hint: count selected edges at each endpoint and at the intermediate vertex (1,1)(1,1)(1,1).

Stars A(0,1)A_{(0,1)}A(0,1)​ and A(1,2)A_{(1,2)}A(1,2)​ each meet one selected Z edge and read −1-1−1. The intermediate A(1,1)A_{(1,1)}A(1,1)​ meets both and returns to +1+1+1. The smooth-side star remains a detector even though it has only three factors. Thus both endpoints remain visible. The other checks stay +1+1+1.

  • Zero would require both endpoint detectors to be absent. Both are retained here.
  • One would require the smooth-side star to be absent. It remains.
  • Two is correct because each endpoint star meets one selected edge.
  • Dependence on LLL would require a global effect. The named local supports already determine both flags.
Your prediction

Panel (a) repeats the Z seed. Panel (b), “Add Z toward the left,” adds h(0,1)h(0,1)h(0,1). The intermediate star A(1,1)A_{(1,1)}A(1,1)​ meets both edges and returns to +1+1+1. At the reached vertex, A(0,1)A_{(0,1)}A(0,1)​ remains a detector. Its single overlap makes it fail. The bulk partner A(1,2)A_{(1,2)}A(1,2)​ remains failed too. Reaching this smooth side has moved the e without absorbing it.

Panel (c) starts a separate X trial on the same seed qubit. Panel (d), “Add X toward the top,” adds h(0,1)h(0,1)h(0,1). The old face B(0,1)B_{(0,1)}B(0,1)​ returns to +1+1+1. The retained top face B(0,0)B_{(0,0)}B(0,0)​ now meets one X and becomes flagged. Its bulk partner B(1,1)B_{(1,1)}B(1,1)​ stays failed. This rough side cannot absorb that m.

On bbb, those counts are two and one. At the corner, each Pauli flags one check. These are individual-edge tests, separate from the extended paths.

Edge a=v(1,0)a=v(1,0)a=v(1,0) belongs to star A(1,1)A_{(1,1)}A(1,1)​ and faces B(0,0),B(1,0)B_{(0,0)},B_{(1,0)}B(0,0)​,B(1,0)​. The absent exterior star contributes no reading. Thus

a:(NX flags under Z,NZ flags under X)=(1,2).a:\quad (N_{X\text{ flags under }Z},N_{Z\text{ flags under }X})=(1,2).a:(NX flags under Z​,NZ flags under X​)=(1,2).

Edge b=v(0,1)b=v(0,1)b=v(0,1) belongs to stars A(0,1),A(0,2)A_{(0,1)},A_{(0,2)}A(0,1)​,A(0,2)​ and face B(0,1)B_{(0,1)}B(0,1)​. The exterior face is absent, so

b:(NX flags under Z,NZ flags under X)=(2,1).b:\quad (N_{X\text{ flags under }Z},N_{Z\text{ flags under }X})=(2,1).b:(NX flags under Z​,NZ flags under X​)=(2,1).

Corner v(0,0)v(0,0)v(0,0) belongs only to A(0,1)A_{(0,1)}A(0,1)​ and B(0,0)B_{(0,0)}B(0,0)​. Consequently,

v(0,0):(NX flags under Z,NZ flags under X)=(1,1).v(0,0):\quad (N_{X\text{ flags under }Z},N_{Z\text{ flags under }X})=(1,1).v(0,0):(NX flags under Z​,NZ flags under X​)=(1,1).

For an extended path, count overlaps with the whole selected support. Its old endpoint check changes from one overlap to two. The sign changes from (−1)1=−1(-1)^1=-1(−1)1=−1 to (−1)2=+1(-1)^2=+1(−1)2=+1. A retained next detector meets one edge and reads −1-1−1; an absent detector supplies no flag. The unchanged bulk partner still meets one edge and remains failed.

Condensation therefore removes the boundary flag while preserving the bulk partner. Rejection leaves both endpoints visible. The side rule applies away from corners; the corner requires its own incidence count.

On the L=3L=3L=3 torus, move the representatives from row or column zero to row or column one by multiplying checks. Use Zˉ1\bar Z_1Zˉ1​ on h(x,1)h(x,1)h(x,1) and Xˉ1\bar X_1Xˉ1​ on h(1,y)h(1,y)h(1,y). Panel (a), “Two periodic joins,” is the L=3L=3L=3 torus. Here LLL counts vertices per periodic row and column. Its seam arrows identify opposite sides. Erasing those arrows alone would leave the old checks acting across the seams. To define an open code, we must change their supports.

Panel (b) deletes h(0,0),h(1,0),h(2,0)h(0,0),h(1,0),h(2,0)h(0,0),h(1,0),h(2,0) and the stars A(0,0),A(1,0),A(2,0)A_{(0,0)},A_{(1,0)},A_{(2,0)}A(0,0)​,A(1,0)​,A(2,0)​. Each retained face acts only on its surviving edges. The vertical join opens into top and bottom Z-boundaries. Only the horizontal join remains; this surface is a cylinder. The construction retains incomplete faces and leaves free ends without stars Quantum codes on a lattice with boundary, PDF pp. 2-3, Figs. 1-2 Original source ↗.

Let nnn count data qubits, NX,NZN_X,N_ZNX​,NZ​ count checks, and rX,rZr_X,r_ZrX​,rZ​ count independent checks. Let k=n−rX−rZk=n-r_X-r_Zk=n−rX​−rZ​ count encoded qubits, as in the CSS count. Deleting three of the torus's eighteen data leaves n=15n=15n=15.

The nine faces still cover every retained edge twice. Their full product remains identity, as in the torus constraints. Shared edges force all face-selection bits to agree, leaving only that dependency and rZ=8r_Z=8rZ​=8. For stars, a dangling edge forces its sole star out of an identity product. Shared edges propagate that exclusion through all six stars. Thus rX=6r_X=6rX​=6 and k=15−6−8=1k=15-6-8=1k=15−6−8=1.

Panel (c), “Inspect the lost pair,” selects the three top faces. Each vertical factor occurs twice and cancels. Their product is the horizontal row: B(0,0)B(1,0)B(2,0)=Zˉ1B_{(0,0)}B_{(1,0)}B_{(2,0)}=\bar Z_1B(0,0)​B(1,0)​B(2,0)​=Zˉ1​. This formerly logical row now acts as +1+1+1 on every cylinder code state. The restricted partner uses h(1,1),h(1,2)h(1,1),h(1,2)h(1,1),h(1,2). It would fail B(1,0)B_{(1,0)}B(1,0)​ and B(1,2)B_{(1,2)}B(1,2)​, so it no longer preserves the code space.

Return to the edge inventory.

§

Count the patch from an explicit edge inventory

Our patch has three vertex columns and three rows of vertical-edge qubits. Call this size d=3d=3d=3. In this family, ddd counts both quantities and can be any integer at least two. It has not yet been identified with distance.

Panel (a) counts horizontal edges. Each retained vertex row has two, giving H=2×2=4H=2\times2=4H=2×2=4. Here HHH names the horizontal tally.

Panel (b) adds interior vertical edges. Three columns each contribute one, giving I=3×1=3I=3\times1=3I=3×1=3. This III is an edge count, distinct from the identity operator.

Panel (c) adds the dangling edges at both ends of each column. Their tally is D=2×3=6D=2\times3=6D=2×3=6. The data count is therefore n=H+I+D=4+3+6=13n=H+I+D=4+3+6=13n=H+I+D=4+3+6=13. Tips and check markers add no data qubits.

Panel (d) counts checks. Each retained vertex carries a star, giving NX=2×3=6N_X=2\times3=6NX​=2×3=6. The middle band has two complete faces. The top and bottom each add two truncated faces, giving NZ=2+2+2=6N_Z=2+2+2=6NZ​=2+2+2=6. Each family has four checks of weight three and two of weight four. A check's weight counts the data qubits it acts on. These counts alone do not establish independence.

Panel (e), “Test star independence,” selects stars for a possible identity product. We reuse the selection-bit argument: one includes a check; zero omits it. In panel (e), λ\lambdaλ is a star's selection bit. Only A(1,1)A_{(1,1)}A(1,1)​ touches v(1,0)v(1,0)v(1,0). Including that star would leave an uncanceled X there, so it must be omitted. The surviving logical pair

Panel (a), “One endpoint remains,” resumes the Z route on v(1,0),v(1,1)v(1,0),v(1,1)v(1,0),v(1,1). Only A(1,2)A_{(1,2)}A(1,2)​ is failed. The probe shares only v(1,1)v(1,1)v(1,1) with the Z column. Their opposite letters anticommute there, giving the logical crossing sign. Every check product commutes with the probe because each check does. The column therefore cannot be a check product. It acts on the encoded qubit even though no check fails Topological quantum memory, PDF p. 7; @bravyi_kitaev_boundary_1998, PDF p. 4 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1063/1.1499754.

Panel (d) multiplies the completed column by B(0,0)B_{(0,0)}B(0,0)​. The repeated Z on v(1,0)v(1,0)v(1,0) cancels, while h(0,1)h(0,1)h(0,1) and v(0,0)v(0,0)v(0,0) join the support. The route becomes {h(0,1),v(0,0),v(1,1),v(1,2)}\{h(0,1),v(0,0),v(1,1),v(1,2)\}{h(0,1),v(0,0),v(1,1),v(1,2)}, with weight four. Its top endpoint moves sideways. The positive check leaves its action on code states unchanged, just as in the torus deformation.

A relative cycle has no detected endpoints because its open ends lie on the matching absorbing sides. Both spanning routes have this property. Closed components are allowed too, since they have no ends to detect.

Panel (e), “Return to the same side,” draws a different support: B(0,0)B_{(0,0)}B(0,0)​ alone. Its route leaves the top and returns to the top. It acts as +1+1+1 on code states. Here we describe Z supports on the primal lattice. A relative boundary is a relative cycle made by multiplying face checks.

Panel (f) counts selected top dangling edges modulo two. The column has one; the deformed column also has one. Their parity is odd. The separate face has two, giving even parity. Every face contains zero or two top dangling edges. Multiplying any faces therefore preserves this parity.

Why does this distinguish every zero-syndrome Z support? The thirteen edge-selection bits obey six independent star constraints, leaving 13−6=713-6=713−6=7 free bits. Six independent face moves identify supports with the same action. They remove six of those choices, leaving 7−6=17-6=17−6=1 class bit and two classes. Top parity is unchanged by face moves and distinguishes the column from identity. It therefore labels both classes completely.

On this hole-free patch, a simple same-side return has zero or two top endpoints and is a relative boundary. An opposite-side path has one and acts logically Topological quantum memory, PDF p. 7; @bravyi_kitaev_boundary_1998, PDF p. 4 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1063/1.1499754. For disconnected relative cycles, add the parities of all components. The classification concerns the whole support.

The CSS logical classes have k=1k=1k=1 independent bit in each pure sector. Every nontrivial pure-X logical belongs to the one nonzero X class. It anticommutes with the Z class, including every column representative. Odd overlap with each disjoint column requires at least one different data qubit per column. Thus its weight is at least ddd.

Every nontrivial pure-Z logical likewise anticommutes with each X row. Disjointness forces at least ddd data qubits in that support too. This argument counts physical qubits, not intersections at check centers.

For a general Pauli PPP, let binary masks x,zx,zx,z specify its X and Z supports. These masks are separate from the drawing coordinates. Up to phase, P∝X(x)Z(z)P\propto X(x)Z(z)P∝X(x)Z(z). An X check tests only the Z mask; a Z check tests only the X mask. Zero syndrome for PPP therefore makes both components commute with every check.

If both components were check products up to phase, PPP would be one too. A nontrivial logical must therefore contain a nontrivial component. With supp⁡\operatorname{supp}supp denoting selected qubits and wt⁡\operatorname{wt}wt their count,

wt⁡(P)=∣supp⁡x∪supp⁡z∣≥max⁡{∣supp⁡x∣,∣supp⁡z∣}≥d.\operatorname{wt}(P) =|\operatorname{supp}x\cup\operatorname{supp}z| \geq\max\{|\operatorname{supp}x|,|\operatorname{supp}z|\} \geq d.wt(P)=∣suppx∪suppz∣≥max{∣suppx∣,∣suppz∣}≥d.

Where the masks overlap, X and Z make Y up to phase. That qubit counts once and never cancels to identity. The spanning witnesses already have weight ddd, proving dcode=dd_{\rm code}=ddcode​=d against all Pauli errors. This is the distance of the specified code with perfect syndrome information.

At d=4d=4d=4, panels (i) and (j) force weight at least four in either sector. Their spanning witnesses attain four, so dcode=4d_{\rm code}=4dcode​=4.

Bound every logical Pauli

Use the disjoint representatives. At size ddd, the patch stores one qubit and has ddd mutually disjoint equivalent Z columns. It also has ddd mutually disjoint equivalent X rows. Each row and column share one qubit. Explain why every nontrivial pure-X and pure-Z logical weighs at least ddd. Then explain why including Y factors cannot lower the full-Pauli distance. Apply the result at d=3d=3d=3 and d=4d=4d=4.

Hint

A nontrivial pure-X logical must anticommute with every representative of the single logical Z class.

Hint

Write a mixed Pauli as X and Z supports; its weight counts their union.

Check against the rubric
  • Uses disjoint representatives for both pure-sector lower bounds.
  • Handles mixed supports and matches the bounds with spanning witnesses.
Show model solution

Odd overlap with each disjoint Z column requires a different qubit in each column. Thus a nontrivial X logical weighs at least ddd. The disjoint X rows give the same bound for a nontrivial Z logical. A mixed zero-syndrome Pauli has separate X and Z components that commute with the checks. If both components are check products, their product is also a check product. Otherwise one component is logical and weighs at least ddd. The union support contains that component, even where both letters combine into Y. The spanning row and column each weigh ddd, so dcode=dd_{\rm code}=ddcode​=d. The two drawn sizes therefore have full-Pauli distances three and four.

Connectivity leaves one full-star dependency, giving rank 9−1=89-1=89−1=8. An outer edge forces its adjacent face out of an identity product. Shared edges propagate that exclusion through the four faces, so their rank is four. Thus k=12−8−4=0k=12-8-4=0k=12−8−4=0. Your answer

The boundary challenge asks how changing the boundary changes this count.

We can now read an endpoint from the retained checks and prove the patch's encoded count and distance. Next we change the cut to keep that distance with fewer data qubits.

Allocate two memories or one

How many data plus measure qubits do two rotated d=5d=5d=5 patches need? Compare your result with one d=7d=7d=7 patch; exclude additional hardware resources.

Two patches use 2(2⋅52−1)=982(2\cdot5^2-1)=982(2⋅52−1)=98 qubits; one d=7d=7d=7 patch uses 97. With independent single-type data errors, perfect checks and minimum-weight recovery, these protect two logical qubits with leading small-ppp order p3p^3p3, versus one with order p4p^4p4. Counts alone do not fix the circuit-level coefficients.

Google uses the same sets of neighboring data qubits for its checks. Exchanging X and Z axes on selected qubits gives its ZXXZ form. Patch anatomy explains this basis choice and the additional hardware. The data and total ratios approach 1/21/21/2. Does equal distance also promise equal error rates?

At d=5d=5d=5, test each five-site Z support for zero syndrome and nontrivial logical action. The unrotated patch has only its five straight columns; the rotated patch has 525252 qualifying site sets. These count logical supports, not failing error patterns. With independent single-type errors, perfect checks, and minimum-weight recovery, fixed odd distance gives the same leading small-ppp power; coefficients can differ. The decoding exercise explores why.

Hadamard exchanges the boundary roles

What if we apply H to every data qubit? Guess whether swapping X and Z leaves this particular check table unchanged.

“Transversal” here means one H on each data site. In (b), HXH=ZHXH=ZHXH=Z and HZH=XHZH=XHZH=X exchange every check's Pauli type. The old names identify the same support lists. Panel (c) reads their new boundary roles; it adds no operation.

H alone changes the group. Old Z-c becomes X1X4X_1X_4X1​X4​, which shares only site 444 with original Z-b and anticommutes with it. An original check product could not do that Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation, PDF p. 31, Sec. XV Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevA.86.032324. How can we return to the original table?

A quarter turn restores the square table, but exchanges what its row and column mean. Panel (d) applies the clockwise spatial map q(r,c)↦q(c,d−1−r)q(r,c)\mapsto q(c,d-1-r)q(r,c)↦q(c,d−1−r), called P↻P_{\circlearrowright}P↻​. Follow the routes:

In the positive sector, or with its signs tracked, the logical actions agree. The symbol ∼\sim∼ expresses that agreement, not identical supports.

The combined operations exchange logical X and Z, giving logical H. Under H alone, the check-data connections stay fixed. Extraction must measure the opposite Pauli products; the implementation determines which gates, bases, or scheduling choices change. Relabeling coordinates does not rotate a device relative to its neighbors; Module 10 develops the physical movement or deformation.

On a three-row, five-column rectangle, the X column has weight three and the Z row weight five. H swaps their Pauli types, taking (dX,dZ)(d_X,d_Z)(dX​,dZ​) from (3,5)(3,5)(3,5) to (5,3)(5,3)(5,3). The separate turn produces five rows and three columns.

We can choose the initial orientation to get the final one we want. Satzinger rotated the logical-zero preparation circuit by 909090 degrees before H Realizing topologically ordered states on a quantum processor, PDF p. 9, supplement Sec. I B Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1126/science.abi8378. Steane's X and Z check spaces coincide, so H already preserves its check group. Can we see the boundary swap without moving sites?

Held fixed
  • Torus lattice coordinates are zero-based: the upper-left vertex is (0,0), x increases rightward, y increases downward, and indices are modulo d. Edge h(x,y) runs right from (x,y); v(x,y) runs down. A(x,y) labels the vertex check, and B(x,y) the plaquette with upper-left corner (x,y).
  • Unrotated planar vertices occupy (d-1) rows and d columns. Top and bottom have d dangling edges apiece. Horizontal edges number (d-1)^2; interior vertical edges number d(d-2).
  • Rotated data qubits are labeled 1..d² row-major. Before a transversal Hadamard, X̄ is a column between the X-boundaries at the top and bottom edges, and Z̄ is a row between the Z-boundaries at the left and right edges. At d=3, X̄ = X₁X₄X₇ and Z̄ = Z₁Z₂Z₃.
  • Rotated bulk faces whose top-left row plus column is even are X, with zero-based coordinates. Weight-2 half-checks on the top and bottom edges are X-type; those on the left and right edges are Z-type before H.
  • One measure qubit per drawn check, including dependent checks. Toric total is 4d^2; planar total is (2d-1)^2; rotated total is 2d^2-1.
Initial conditions
A joint +1 eigenstate of the original checks, optionally transformed by H on every data qubit, followed by the selected Pauli support. The all-smooth layout has one stabilizer state and no encoded qubit.
Boundary conditions
Torus is periodic in both directions. Cylinder is periodic vertically with smooth left/right sides, d by d vertices and 2d^2-d edges. Planar is rough top/bottom and smooth left/right. Rotated uses X top/bottom and Z left/right half-checks before H. All-smooth is a d by d vertex disk with every edge ending on a vertex.
Computed checks and boundary syndrome
Data qubits, reduced-weight checks, Pauli support and flagged checks. Boundary labels give geometry and current check type; rotated boundaries give only check type. Readouts show rank, k, distance method, and data plus measure count. Rotated logical patterns also show their computed qubit support and column or row direction under the current Pauli assignment. The two-error example displays the original error and reports the lookup syndrome, minimum-weight corrections, chosen correction, residual support, residual class, and residual syndrome weight. Horizontal: Horizontal lattice coordinate (lattice spacings). Vertical: Vertical coordinate increasing downward (lattice spacings).
Computed qubit counts versus distance
Formula curves for toric, unrotated and rotated codes at odd d from 3 through 9, plus two operating-point markers for the selected layout. Cylinder and disk markers are calculated from their own incidence structures and are not additional distance curves. Horizontal: Odd distance d (dimensionless). Vertical: Data or data plus measure (qubits).

Method: Build explicit edge/check incidences for each cellulation, with half-checks for the rotated code. Exact integer bit sets give anticommutation and Gaussian-elimination ranks. At d=3 enumerate every X and Z support below the first nontrivial normalizer found; CSS decomposition proves this suffices for general Pauli distance. Larger distance readouts use the straight-string and disjoint-representative bound. Tests additionally search every rotated d=5 X and Z support up to weight 4. Random errors use mulberry32 with independent error draws followed by uniform Pauli draws. The two-error example enumerates every pure-X support on rotated d=3, retains all minimum-weight supports matching the Z-check syndrome, and chooses the lowest binary mask in a tie. Without H, X7 and X8 tie; the lookup chooses X7.

Tolerances: All parity, weight, rank, and support-search results use exact integer arithmetic. No continuum approximation or numerical integration occurs.

Display conventions

  • All readouts and curves are computed. Sizes and error patterns are illustrative; the 17, 49 and 97 totals are mathematical counts, not measurements of a processor.
  • Select any check by pointer or keyboard to inspect its complete qubit list and weight. This temporary selection resets when controls change.
  • Unrotated qubits are circles on edges, X checks are filled squares and Z checks hollow squares. Z errors use dashed strokes and X errors solid strokes. Flagged checks carry an additional circular outline.
  • Anyon names follow primal location: e is a vertex (star) defect and m is a plaquette defect, regardless of the current check Pauli type. Defect circles are filled for e and hollow for m. Rotated faces and half-checks retain their primal star or plaquette identity when the Paulis swap.
  • Rotated faces use different hatch patterns for X and Z; weight-2 boundary checks are semicircles. Nothing geometrically rough or smooth remains in this drawing.
  • Rotated check names match the anatomy figure: bulk checks in reading order, followed by top/bottom or left/right half-checks. At d=3 these are X-a through X-d and Z-a through Z-d. Names stay attached to their supports after H; the current Pauli type is shown separately.
  • For primal Z chains in the unrotated drawing before swapping, with endpoints compared relative to the absorbing boundary, stabilizer equivalence means that the symmetric difference is a boundary (a sum of plaquette boundaries, possibly with several components).
  • Short absorbed strings still have one detected bulk end. Rejected strings have both ends detected. Pattern names keep their geometric direction when the Pauli assignment swaps.
  • At corners an edge can touch both boundary types; anticommutation is always computed from its actual check support. All-smooth corner stars have weight 2, side stars weight 3.
  • Smooth/primal and rough/dual describe the primal drawing, consistent with Browne lecture notes, PDF pp. 102-104. The labels X-boundary and Z-boundary here name the truncated checks.

Commit your prediction above to start the lab, or skip it.

Model limits

Code-capacity snapshots only; no circuit faults, measurement errors, or repeated rounds. Only the two-error example applies a minimum-weight pure-X lookup with perfect syndrome; random samples have no recovery decoder.

Counts assume a dedicated measure qubit per check and exclude routing, leakage removal, spare qubits, and scheduling overhead.

The all-smooth disk has k=0, so a logical distance is undefined. Its size parameter and count markers must not be interpreted as a protected-memory distance.

The cylinder is a specified smooth-boundary cellulation, not a claim that cutting any hardware torus automatically produces these checks.

A measure qubit must be able to reach every data qubit on its check's list. Follow one check's links before counting the whole patch.

A coupler graph has a vertex for each data or measure qubit and a link for each required check-data interaction. Panel (a)'s bulk check needs four links. Count the required interactions

How many check-data couplings does a rotated d=7d=7d=7 patch require, counting one link for every data qubit in every check?

Explanation

There are 36 weight-four checks and 12 weight-two checks: 36⋅4+12⋅2=168=4⋅7⋅636\cdot4+12\cdot2=168=4\cdot7\cdot636⋅4+12⋅2=168=4⋅7⋅6. This is a connectivity count; a specific extraction circuit must still schedule those interactions.

The d=7d=7d=7 graph has 49+48=9749+48=9749+48=97 code qubits. Four leakage-removal extras give 101101101 allocated on Google's cited 105105105-qubit processor; these extras are not checks Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold, PDF pp. 1, 2, Fig. 1 Original source ↗ · DOI: 10.1038/s41586-024-08449-y. Using each link for one two-qubit operation gives 168168168 operations, not circuit depth or the chip's full coupler inventory. Module 7 supplies circuits and error budgets.

We can now read syndromes, track preparation signs, correct logical readout, follow H, and count interactions. Try the practice; reliability with faulty repeated circuits remains Module 7's question.

4.4 · Reconstruct and transfer

Start with the cutting reconstruction, Hadamard, then decoding. Allow about 40 minutes. The remaining frame, rectangle and boundary exercises are optional extensions.

Cut the torus in the opposite order

Use the L=3L=3L=3 toric code: qubits lie on edges h(x,y)h(x,y)h(x,y) and v(x,y)v(x,y)v(x,y), with coordinates modulo three. X stars act on edges meeting a vertex; Z faces act around a square. Keep the original edge convention.

Turn off one check

If one check goes silent, where can an error end without being seen? Keep all data and perfect remaining measurements.

  1. Remove Z-a from the canonical d=3d=3d=3 patch. Find ranks, kkk, single-site logicals, and distance protecting all information.
  2. At d=5d=5d=5, remove Z-c on 6,7,11,126,7,11,126,7,11,12. Find the full-code X/Z distances and the added logical pair.
  3. Now choose a gauge qubit, an encoded degree of freedom whose state we choose not to protect. Pair the missing Z check with the shortest X path to the nearer X-boundary. The dressed distance is the least physical weight of a protected logical action when arbitrary action on that gauge qubit is allowed. Specify a protected pair commuting with the gauge pair. Derive X/Z distances at d=3,5d=3,5d=3,5, comparing missing-face rows.
  4. What sets the perimeter logical weight of a genuine m×mm\times mm×m hole? Why enlarge it?
  5. Do 494949 data and 979797 data-plus-measure qubits certify distance on a defective patch?

Hint

Removing an independent check releases one binary constraint.

Hint

Its conjugate can be a boundary-to-hole X string crossing the missing check once.

Hint

Decompose an unflagged X support into paths between the two absorbing boundaries and the missing face. Bound each connection by how many face rows it must cross.

Draw an unflagged X support as dual paths. Its ends can lie only on the top boundary, bottom boundary, or missing face; closed local detours can be removed by star checks. There are three nontrivial connection classes: top to bottom, top to hole, and bottom to hole. Count crossed data sites. A step advances by at most one face row. For Z-c in face row 1, reaching the top therefore needs at least two sites and reaching the bottom at least three. Tangent: a hole is an internal boundary

Optional. In an all-smooth disk, omitting one independent face check changes k=0k=0k=0 to k=1k=1k=1. The missing Z check is the new logical Z; an X path from it to the exterior is its conjugate. With shortest path length DpD_pDp​, distance is min⁡(4,Dp)\min(4,D_p)min(4,Dp​).

On a 5×55\times55×5 vertex disk, face (1,1)(1,1)(1,1) gives (dX,dZ)=(2,4)(d_X,d_Z)=(2,4)(dX​,dZ​)=(2,4); corner (0,0)(0,0)(0,0) gives (1,4)(1,4)(1,4). On a 6×66\times66×6 disk, face (2,2)(2,2)(2,2) gives (3,4)(3,4)(3,4). A genuine m×mm\times mm×m square hole of this same smooth type has Z perimeter weight 4m4m4m. With an all-smooth exterior, hhh disjoint smooth holes encode hhh qubits. Perimeter and separation both limit protection. §

Which connections does a memory need?

What did opening and trimming the lattice change?

The retained checks determine where a string may end without a flag. Their independent ranks determine how many qubits are encoded. Logical strings then tell us the distance. A smaller rotated patch keeps that distance while using fewer data qubits.

On a numbered patch, we can now follow a syndrome, track a Pauli frame, and distinguish data qubits from qubits used to measure checks. The connection count describes the patch; it does not yet tell us its reliability under faulty gates.

Module 5 asks what changes when checks connect qubits beyond nearby lattice sites.
